priority.description: Priority order when recommending Dialtone solutions

details.component: Always prefer specific Vue components when one fits the use case (e.g., DtButton over composing a button manually)
details.primitive: When no specific component fits, reach for the primitive triad — DtBox (surface, padding, border, shadow, sizing, simple token-backed positioning), DtStack (layout: direction, gap, alignment), DtText (typography) — before composing with utility classes
details.utility-class: Use utility classes for styling concerns the primitives intentionally don't cover (display, grid, flex-child), for positioning outside DtBox's prop surface (responsive, calc, reset, arbitrary coordinates, non-DtBox elements), or for surgical adjustments (e.g., d-pr2 for padding-right)
details.token: Use design tokens for custom CSS implementations when components, primitives, and utilities don't fit

details.semantic: Prefer semantic color tokens (e.g., --dt-color-foreground-primary, --dt-color-surface-positive) over base colors. Components and primitives like DtBox already use semantic tokens internally — these guidelines apply when you're writing raw CSS.
details.base: Use base color tokens (e.g., --dt-color-purple-600) only when semantic colors don't fit the use case

details.dt-text: In Vue templates, prefer the DtText component for any text — it handles family, kind (headline/body/label), size, weight, and tone via validated props (e.g., <dt-text kind="body" :size="200">). Part of the primitive triad alongside DtBox and DtStack.
details.typography-class: Use typography utility classes (e.g., d-body--md-compact) or complete typography tokens (e.g., --dt-typography-body-md) for non-Vue HTML or as a class escape hatch when DtText doesn't fit
details.text-style-token: Use individual text style tokens (e.g., --dt-font-size-200, --dt-line-height-100) only for fine-tuned control in custom CSS

search.description: How to search Dialtone documentation effectively
tips: Search by CSS property names: Dialtone utilities apply logical properties internally, so prefer logical names ('padding-block-start', 'margin-inline-end') over physical ('padding-top', 'margin-right'); physical queries surface noisy results

Search by class name patterns (e.g., 'pbs-200', 'mie-100', 'd-flex'). Logical abbrevs: pbs/pbe (block-start/end), pis/pie (inline-start/end). Legacy 'pt'/'pr' aliases still emit but apply logical properties under the hood
Search by component API — the search indexes prop names, slot names, and event names (e.g., 'startIcon' for a prop, 'header' for a slot, 'update:open' for an event)
Use specific technical terms rather than natural language
